skill.name: Fix tense slips
skill.why: When verbs jump between times, readers lose track of when things happened.
skill.how: Find the time clue. Check each verb fits it. True facts can stay in the present.

steps.say: Every verb tells when. First, I find the time clue.

show.nudge: Mo is who, and burnt is what he did. Which word tells you when?
The toast is the thing he burnt. Which word tells you when?

steps.ask: Tap the word that tells you when.
steps.win: Yes! Yesterday is over, so the verbs should be past.

steps.say: I check each verb against yesterday. Then, or now?

steps.ask: Tap the verb in the wrong time.
steps.win: Yes! Fills should be filled. Wrong time: a tense slip.

steps.say: Mo did it again. Say each verb with yesterday.

Burns is happening now. Yesterday is over.

creature.name: Clinkit
creature.blurb: A cinder-coloured beetle that trundles along one warm crack in the volcano's rock and never steps off it. It keeps a story's verbs on one track of time.

write.ask: Rewrite Gus's diary so each verb fits yesterday. Leave the true fact in the present.
given: Yesterday, Gus drops a jar of slime.
It splats all over the kitchen floor.
Slime is very hard to clean.
checks: Every verb about yesterday is now past.
I didn't use has with yesterday.
I left the true fact in the present.
write.model: Yesterday, Gus dropped a jar of slime. It splatted all over the kitchen floor. Slime is very hard to clean.
